items.prompt: This is an order-3 B-tree (2 keys per branch). You insert 10. Where does it go?
hints: Start at the root. Is 10 smaller or larger than 20?
New keys always go into a leaf, in sorted order.
10 < 20, so go left to [8]. The leaf has room: it becomes [8, 10].

options.feedback: Right. 10 < 20 sends us left, and [8] has room for a second key.
New keys always go into a leaf. Keys only reach the root by moving up during a split.
10 < 20, so the search goes left at the root.

items.prompt: This is an order-3 B-tree (2 keys per branch). You insert 25. Which key moves up to the parent?
hints: Put 25 into the right leaf first. How many keys does that branch hold now?
An order-3 branch holds at most 2 keys. With 3 keys it snaps, and the middle key moves up.
The leaf becomes [25, 28, 30]. The middle key is 28, so 28 moves up next to 20.

items.prompt: This is an order-3 B-tree (2 keys per branch). You insert 25. Which key moves up to the parent?
hints: Put 25 into the right leaf first. How many keys does that branch hold now?
An order-3 branch holds at most 2 keys. With 3 keys it snaps, and the middle key moves up.
The leaf becomes [25, 28, 30]. The middle key, 28, moves up next to 20.

options.feedback: Not quite. The key that moves up is the middle one after insertion, not the new one.
Yes. After 25 goes in, the branch holds 25, 28 and 30, and the middle key moves up.

options.text: 30, the largest key in the branch
options.feedback: Not quite. After 25 goes in, the branch holds 25, 28 and 30. The middle key moves up, not the largest.

options.text: No key moves up, because the leaf has room
options.feedback: The leaf already holds 2 keys, the maximum for order 3. A third key makes it overflow.

items.prompt: You insert 70 into this order-3 tree. What happens to its height?
hints: Which leaf does 70 go into, and does it overflow?
When a key moves up into a full parent, the parent splits too.
[50, 60, 70] splits and 60 moves up. The root [20, 40, 60] splits and 40 becomes a new root: height 2 → 3.

options.text: It grows by one level, at the root
options.feedback: Yes. The split cascades to the root, a new root appears, and every leaf moves down together.

options.text: It grows by one level, under the leaf
options.feedback: That is how a binary search tree grows. A B-tree only grows at the top, so all leaves stay level.
The leaf split pushes 60 into the root, which overflows and splits too.

items.prompt: Is this a valid order-3 B-tree?
hints: Look at where each leaf sits.
In a B-tree every leaf is on the same level.
